audit: Full notification subsystem correctness and functional inspection

interfaces_inspected: backend/app.py notification router binding and export exclusion
backend/http_transport.py cancellable bounded HTTP interface and shared-loop resolver lifecycle
pywebpush.webpush and WebPusher session injection, encryption, VAPID signing and error response behavior
areas: whole-request deadlines through shared bounded HTTP
finite notification batch-start budget and durable deferral

findings.problem: Queued messages could be resurrected after a pause/resume during an existing delivery batch, and queueing could race a pause.
findings.root_cause: Batch claims unconditionally updated stale snapshots; queue enablement was read outside the mutation transaction.
findings.repair: Claim current queued/retry status and channel enablement in the same write transaction, reread attempts, and recheck queue enablement inside its insert transaction.

findings.problem: New or resumed browser recipients could receive prior uncollected history; unsubscribed pending items could resume after resubscription.
findings.root_cause: Only a channel-wide event cursor existed, and unsubscribe did not cancel pending recipient rows.
findings.repair: Add durable recipient baseline_event_id, preserve the baseline for active key updates, baseline new/resumed recipients, and atomically fail queued/retry items on unsubscribe.

findings.problem: A webhook accepting delivery with a valid non-object JSON response was recorded unknown.
findings.root_cause: Accepted response bodies were assumed to have a get method.
findings.repair: Treat accepted HTTP status as webhook acceptance and read an optional remote ID only from object bodies.

findings.problem: Safe media PUT retries were lost on provider 5xx, and valid HTTP 201 upload acceptance was rejected.
findings.root_cause: Retry classification only considered read operations and the PUT acceptance set omitted Created.
findings.repair: Classify read and idempotent PUT 5xx as retryable, accept 200/201/204 for PUT, and reuse persisted media/upload identity on retries.

findings.problem: Delivery and operator reconciliation statuses could commit without their matching receipt, or an acceptance receipt could survive without final status.
findings.root_cause: Receipt inserts and status writes used separate transactions.
findings.repair: Persist each terminal/retry delivery receipt with its outbox state and each operator reconciliation receipt with its status in one transaction.

findings.problem: An inability to open the lock file permanently left the in-process dispatcher busy.
findings.root_cause: The mutex was acquired before an open call outside the try/finally cleanup.
findings.repair: Acquire the file inside the cleanup scope and release the mutex even if open or close fails.

findings.problem: A slow external call consumed the configured retry delay, causing the next retry to become due immediately.
findings.root_cause: The clock was frozen at batch entry and used after transport completion.
findings.repair: Keep explicit test clocks deterministic but recompute production time at collection, claims, and completion; backoff starts at completion.

findings.problem: Malformed channel values or malformed HTTPS addresses raised internal exceptions rather than validation errors.
findings.root_cause: Set membership ran before channel type validation, and URL parsing/port validation was not guarded.
findings.repair: Validate channel type before membership and return false for malformed addresses/ports.

findings.problem: A terminal failed local notice left after a channel pause blocked acknowledgement of all later delivered notices.
findings.root_cause: The reader cursor treated terminal failed rows as pending.
findings.repair: Allow the delivered-notice reader cursor past terminal failed rows while still rejecting pending/unknown gaps and backward/out-of-range movement.

findings.problem: Changed persisted image bytes could be uploaded while receipts claimed the original content hash.
findings.root_cause: The recorded image digest was never checked at delivery.
findings.repair: Decode and verify the persisted digest before media creation or upload; fail before any provider effect on mismatch.

findings.problem: Typefully silently truncated an explicit message to 280 characters while the acceptance receipt omitted the modification.
findings.root_cause: The text slice did not record transmitted length/scope.
findings.repair: Preserve the original outbox payload and disclose original/transmitted character counts in the acceptance receipt when truncated.

findings.problem: HTTP error responses were returned without closing their response stream.
findings.root_cause: The HTTPError branch bypassed the success response context manager.
findings.repair: The urllib response-error path was first closed explicitly, then replaced by shared bounded_http whose async response/client context closes all transport resources. Status handling and retry/ambiguity semantics are preserved.

findings.problem: Two dispatcher instances addressing one SQLite database through a file symlink could bypass the process lock.
findings.root_cause: Lock-file names were derived from the supplied path instead of its resolved database path.
findings.repair: Resolve the database path before naming the notification lock and retain the atomic SQL claim guard.

findings.problem: A restart with a different webhook URL or Typefully social set could redirect a previously approved pending/retry message.
findings.root_cause: Persisted enablement and queued items were bound only to the channel name.
findings.repair: Persist an opaque receiver binding, pause changed receivers, fail their prior queued/retry rows, baseline future events upon explicit enablement, and guard delivery against receiver drift; same-receiver credential rotation preserves existing authorization.

findings.problem: Socket idle timeouts allowed a provider continuously dribbling response bytes to stall the shared operations worker indefinitely, including WebPush requests through requests/pywebpush.
findings.root_cause: urllib and requests timeout values limited inactivity rather than the complete response, so each arriving chunk reset the effective wait.
findings.repair: Route notification HTTP through shared bounded_http with an eight-second whole-request deadline, 256000-byte limit and redirects disabled. Inject a bounded session adapter into real pywebpush, preserving its encryption/VAPID signing and accepted/expired status handling. Timeout/oversize POSTs remain unknown and are never automatically replayed. Shared helper cancellation closes the actual HTTP operation rather than abandoning a sender thread.
findings.independent_reproduction: Root final recheck observed a 93-byte dribbling POST response taking 9.032 seconds through the previous eight-second socket timeout. This notification suite independently verifies a real loopback dribble is stopped under a 0.15-second test deadline; no external destination is contacted.

findings.problem: A batch of twelve slow notifications could monopolize the operations worker for hundreds of seconds even after individual network requests became bounded.
findings.root_cause: The dispatcher limited item count without limiting the elapsed time before starting another item; Typefully media can perform four sequential calls per item.
findings.repair: Use a sixteen-second monotonic budget for starting another batch item. Finish the current item and its durable outcome, then leave remaining items queued/retrying for the next pass; report budget_exhausted and the actual deferred_due count. No already accepted publication stage is interrupted or blindly replayed.
findings.timing_scope: This is a start budget, not a whole-runtime deadline. The last item may run beyond the sixteen-second start budget; a Typefully media item can perform up to four bounded eight-second requests, plus local SQL/encryption work.

pre_repair_replay.method: git HEAD:backend/notifications.py evaluated only in an isolated Python process; every test uses a temporary SQLite database and mocked transports
pre_repair_replay.scope_note: Historical first audit baseline before the HTTP-deadline follow-up: 29 exercised tests, 16 failure entries and 5 error entries. New deadline/helper regressions were added afterward and do not alter that historical replay log.

verification.databases: Per-test TemporaryDirectory SQLite files; default desk database untouched
verification.transport_probe: One real loopback HTTP POST per suite execution; external endpoints never contacted. WebPush cryptography executes with locally generated fixture keys and a mocked bounded transport.

preserved_contracts: External channels remain opt-in and disabled in an empty installation.
Provider acceptance remains distinct from audience/browser/X publication.
Ambiguous POSTs and interrupted external sends stay unknown and are never automatically replayed.
Retry requires definite failure/retry state; unknown outcomes need an explicit factual reconciliation.
Per-recipient idempotent outbox uniqueness remains channel/event/recipient.
No trade strategies or order-creation authority were added.
Existing subscription migration preserves recipient IDs and pending scope; initial receiver-binding migration preserves existing channel enablement.
limits: External destinations remain simulated; only the dribble deadline regression uses a real loopback HTTP server. Real WebPush cryptography executes with generated fixture keys and a mocked transport. No live webhook, Typefully or browser-push credentials/delivery were tested.
An external channel paused or changed during an already submitted request cannot retract that in-flight request; its actual acceptance outcome is recorded.
Unknown external delivery still requires destination reconciliation; exactly-once audience delivery cannot be inferred from HTTP acceptance.

On the first migration of a previously unbound legacy channel, the current configured environment is recorded as its receiver; historical receiver values were never persisted and cannot be independently reconstructed.
Receiver bindings are opaque hashes and contain no raw endpoints or credentials in snapshots.
The file lock assumes cooperating processes on one local filesystem; arbitrary hard-linked database aliases and uncoordinated lock-file deletion are outside the supported deployment.
PNG queue validation checks a bounded PNG signature; image decoding/processing remains the provider responsibility.
X message truncation remains at 280 characters and is now explicitly disclosed in the delivery receipt.

HTTP request deadlines are separate from the sixteen-second batch-start budget. A current item may finish its bounded stages after the start budget; the complete operations cycle has no asserted hard time limit.

The shared HTTP helper uses a cancellable IO loop and at most four resolver threads. A cancelled DNS lookup may finish later, but its result cannot initiate a late HTTP request; helper-owned tests verify a delayed lookup resolving to a real loopback server produces no late POST.
